_meta.note: A throw inside the per-recipient send path must release its semaphore slot and count as a failed recipient, not wedge the semaphore and 500 the whole batch. This is the ONE place the rewrite deliberately changes the Ghost-facing wire contract: the same request returns 500 today. Do not capture the current response.
_meta.currentBehavior: lib/send-email.js:204 acquires a slot but chains release() onto sendRawEmail(...).finally(). Anything throwing before that call (substituteVars, buildRawMime, JSON.stringify, Buffer.from) rejects the .then callback without releasing. Promise.all rejects, the handler's outer catch returns 500 {message: 'Internal server error: ...'}, the successful sends are dropped from the response, and the slot is gone. After SEND_CONCURRENCY such failures every subsequent send hangs forever with no response, no log, and /health still 200.

inducedFailure.how: The test forces a synchronous throw inside the per-recipient callback body — i.e. inside runExclusive's callback and outside the SES promise chain. Stubbing buildRawMime (or substituteVars) to throw for this one recipient reproduces the real D1 path. A rejected SES promise does NOT exercise this defect; the current code already handles that case correctly.

subsequentSendSucceeds.note: Repeat the same request with no induced failure. It must return 200 and not hang. Run it at least sendConcurrency times so a leaked slot cannot hide behind spare capacity.

allRecipientsThrow.note: When EVERY recipient throws before its SES call, the batch is a total failure and keeps the existing failure shape — the errors[] array is populated from the thrown messages rather than from SES rejections.
